chunks: And with this chain, from Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), that he said: He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
Whoever gives legal verdicts to the people without knowledge, the angels of the heavens and the earth will curse him.

key_terms.أَفْتَى: Issued a legal verdict or fatwa

ai.seo_question: What is the consequence for giving religious rulings without knowledge?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* underscores the critical Shia emphasis on *'ilam* (certainty) and *'adl* (justice) in jurisprudence, warning that unqualified *ifta'* incurs a universal curse from the angels of the heavens and earth. It serves as a foundational principle for distinguishing between true scholars (*mujtahids*) and those who issue arbitrary opinions, reinforcing the authority of the Ahl al-Bayt's teachings in validating religious knowledge.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 31-173 According to the same documentation, it is narrated that Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) quoted on the authority of God’s Prophet (S), “
The angels in the heavens and the Earth will damn anyone who makes a decree for the people without having knowledge.”
